children: Bitcoin
Layer 2 solution
Liquid Network
said on Sunday that white-hat hackers drained BTC worth tens of millions from the platform.
What Exactly Happened
Liquid Network stated on X that hackers withdrew nearly 4,000 BTC worth $320 million and that it has paused all bridge activity and new transactions.

“Bridge nodes have been temporarily disabled, so no new transactions can be submitted to the network. Effectively, the Liquid sidechain is paused until this issue is resolved,” the platform announced.
Liquid platform said it has alerted exchanges that have halted deposits of
Liquid Bitcoin
(LBTC)—a tokenized, 1:1 BTC-backed asset native to the platform.
“Liquid wallets will be impacted, and we’re sorry for any inconvenience. Federation members are actively working on resolving this so we can restore normal network activity,” it added.
We are aware of a security incident on
. Purported white-hat hackers have withdrawn ~4,000 BTC (~$320 million) from the Liquid Federation wallet. The
team is working on contacting them on-chain with a signed message.
What we know so far is that the funds…
‘Contact Us On Chain’
The exploit resulted in the loss of nearly 95% of Liquid Network’s reported Bitcoin reserves, according to the Mempool tracker released by the platform.
The hackers left an on-chain message, saying, “We are whitehats. contact us on chain.”
White hat hackers, also known as ethical hackers or security professionals, use their knowledge to identify and fix vulnerabilities in computer systems.
Liquid Network didn’t immediately return Benzinga’s request for comment.
